newsitem.title: MEXICO: POLL - Kimberly-Clark Mexico Q2 to trail year-ago.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Kimberly-Clark Mexico Q2 to trail year-ago.

text.p: Paper producer Kimberly Clark de Mexico will show improved results in the second quarter of the year compared with the first quarter, benefitting from better operating margins, analysts said, but second quarter results this year will not be as good as in the same quarter last year.
"We will see a reversal in the weakening trend seen in the last three or four quarters, as much in sales as in margins," said Michel Morin, an analyst with Merrill Lynch.

A survey of four analysts found an average forecast of a profit of 0.4033 peso per share in the second quarter, above the 0.26 peso profit seen in the first quarter but below the 0.45 peso per share profit seen in the second quarter of last year.
They also forecast revenues of 2.491 billion pesos in the second quarter of this year, compared with 2.79 billion in the second quarter last year and 2.126 billion in the first quarter of this year.

Operating profit in the second quarter of this year is seen at 621 million pesos, compared with 760 million in the second quarter of last year and 481 million pesos in the first quarter of this year. Net profits in the second quarter are
seen at 622 million pesos compared with year-earlier second quarter net profits of 620 million pesos and first quarter net profits of 363 million pesos.
An analyst with brokerage house Valores Finamex, Jesus Viveros, noted that Easter Week fell in the first quarter this year, unlike last year, when it fell in the second quarter.
"There will be an important improvement... due basically to the fact that during the first quarter there was a strong influence from Easter Week," said Viveros.
Analysts said part of the blame for weaker year-over-year results in the second quarter this year could be tied to lower levels of consumption and lower product prices in Mexico.
Moreover, paper prices are lower on an international level, they said.
John Chan, with Goldman Sachs in New York, said sales of Kimberly could fall 13 percent in the second quarter from the same quarter last year, due to lower prices.
However, analysts said the company will show continuing improvement in the second half of the year and onward as the Mexican economy improves.
The forecasts do not include extraordinary revenues derived from the sale of certain assets to Grupe Copamex.
The company is an affiliate of Kimberly-Clark Corp of the U.S.
